name: SDD Specification Template (Balanced 4-Phase Structure)
description: Comprehensive specification template based on SDD methodology with balanced 4-phase structure optimal workload distribution

primaryUserStory.title: Primary User Story
primaryUserStory.instruction: Describe the main user journey in plain language, focusing on business value and user outcomes

comprehensiveUserStories.title: Comprehensive User Stories
comprehensiveUserStories.instruction: Generate 8-10 user stories covering different user personas, roles, and scenarios. Use format: **As a [user type], I want [goal] so that [benefit]**. Follow INVEST criteria: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small (sprint-sized), Testable. Include: 1) Primary user story, 2) Admin/Manager story, 3) Power user story, 4) New user story, 5) Edge case user story, 6) Integration user story, 7) Mobile user story (if applicable), 8) Accessibility user story. Each story should be sprint-sized and deliverable.

acceptanceScenarios.title: Acceptance Scenarios
acceptanceScenarios.instruction: Generate comprehensive acceptance criteria using Given-When-Then format. Include: 1) Happy path scenarios (primary user flows), 2) Negative scenarios (error conditions, invalid inputs), 3) Edge cases (boundary conditions, unusual inputs), 4) User perspective focus (desired outcomes, not implementation), 5) Testable criteria (clear pass/fail outcomes), 6) Stakeholder scenarios (admin, power user, new user perspectives). Each scenario should be independently testable and written in simple, unambiguous language. Generate sufficient scenarios to cover all critical functionalities and edge cases without redundancy. Use numbered list format (1., 2., 3.) for Happy Path Scenarios to ensure proper Markdown rendering.

edgeCases.title: Edge Cases
edgeCases.instruction: List boundary conditions and error scenarios: - What happens when [boundary condition]? - How does the system handle [error scenario]?

functionalRequirements.title: Functional Requirements
functionalRequirements.instruction: Generate comprehensive functional requirements using FR-001, FR-002 format. Follow best practices: 1) Clear and concise language (simple, unambiguous), 2) Business goal alignment (each requirement serves specific user need), 3) Consistency (avoid contradictions, use consistent terminology), 4) Verifiability (testable and measurable outcomes), 5) Necessity (essential for system functionality). Include: Core functionality, User interactions, Data operations, System behaviors, Business rules, Integration requirements. Each requirement should be independently testable and traceable to user stories. Generate adequate requirements to describe all necessary system behaviors without overcomplicating.

keyEntities.title: Key Entities
keyEntities.instruction: List data entities if feature involves data: - **[Entity 1]** — [What it represents, key attributes] - **[Entity 2]** — [What it represents, relationships]

databaseRequirements.title: Database Requirements
databaseRequirements.instruction: AI must choose appropriate production-ready database based on project requirements. Use SAME database for both development and production. 🚨 CRITICAL: SQLite is FORBIDDEN for any project. Choose from: PostgreSQL (preferred for relational/ACID), MongoDB (for documents), MySQL (for web apps), Redis (for caching). Consider: - **Database Type**: [PostgreSQL for relational/ACID, MongoDB for documents, MySQL for web apps, Redis for caching] - **Data Volume**: [Expected records, growth rate] - **Performance**: [Response time, throughput requirements] - **Consistency**: [ACID, eventual consistency, etc.] - **Security**: [Authentication, encryption, access control] - **Scalability**: [Horizontal/vertical scaling needs] - **Backup/Recovery**: [RTO/RPO requirements] - **Justification**: [Explain why this database is optimal for this project]

uiDesignRequirements.title: UI/Design System Requirements
uiDesignRequirements.instruction: Extract and specify comprehensive design system requirements with platform-specific guidelines: **DESIGN SYSTEM MANDATE**: Extract and specify comprehensive design system requirements, **MODERN UI MANDATE**: Require modern, sophisticated UI design (NO basic/plain designs), **STYLING FRAMEWORK**: Specify exact styling frameworks (Tailwind CSS, Material-UI, Chakra UI, NativeWind, etc.), **DESIGN PATTERNS**: Define modern UI patterns (cards, gradients, shadows, animations, micro-interactions), **VISUAL HIERARCHY**: Specify typography, spacing, color schemes, and visual hierarchy, **RESPONSIVE DESIGN**: Define responsive breakpoints and mobile-first approach, **ACCESSIBILITY**: Include accessibility requirements (WCAG compliance), **BRAND CONSISTENCY**: Define brand colors, fonts, and visual identity, **USER EXPERIENCE**: Specify UX patterns, navigation, and interaction flows, **ANTI-SIMPLE-DESIGN RULE**: Explicitly prohibit basic, plain, or minimal designs. **PLATFORM-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS**: For mobile platforms (iOS, Android, React Native), include: **iOS (SwiftUI/Native)**: Follow Apple Human Interface Guidelines (HIG) - use SF Pro font family, system colors, native navigation patterns (NavigationStack, TabView), proper use of List, Form, and native iOS components, respect safe areas, use native iOS animations and transitions, implement proper haptic feedback, follow iOS spacing and sizing conventions (44pt minimum touch targets), use native iOS design patterns (sheets, alerts, action sheets), implement proper dark mode support, **Android (Native/Kotlin)**: Follow Material Design 3 guidelines - use Material You theming, Material Components (MaterialButton, MaterialCard, etc.), proper elevation and shadows, Material motion animations, use Material Design color system, implement proper navigation (Navigation Component), respect system bars and edge-to-edge design, use Material Design typography scale, implement proper Ripple effects, follow Material Design spacing (8dp grid), **React Native (Cross-platform)**: Use platform-specific design tokens, implement platform-specific components (Platform.select for iOS/Android differences), use React Native Paper or NativeBase for Material Design, or React Native Elements for cross-platform components, implement proper navigation (React Navigation with platform-specific styling), use NativeWind or styled-components for styling, respect platform-specific spacing and sizing, implement platform-specific animations (Animated API or Reanimated), use platform-specific icons (react-native-vector-icons), implement proper safe area handling (react-native-safe-area-context), follow platform-specific gesture patterns, ensure proper platform-specific accessibility (AccessibilityInfo, accessibilityLabel)

technologyStack.title: Technology Stack Requirements
technologyStack.instruction: Extract ALL technologies mentioned in the user input and organize them by category. Include: - **Frontend**: [Any frontend technologies mentioned] - **Backend**: [Any backend technologies mentioned] - **Styling**: [Any styling approaches mentioned] - **Charts**: [Any chart libraries mentioned] - **State Management**: [Any state management mentioned] - **Database**: [Any database mentioned] - **Other**: [Any other technologies mentioned] - **Validation Checklist**: [Create checklist to verify all technologies are used]

architecture.instruction: Detect and document the backend architecture pattern from the tech stack and user input. Patterns: - **BaaS (Firebase)**: Client-side SDKs, Security Rules, no server-side controllers - **BaaS (Supabase)**: Client-side PostgREST, RLS policies, no server-side controllers - **BaaS (AWS Amplify)**: Client-side AppSync, IAM policies - **Traditional Backend**: Express/FastAPI controllers, service layers, REST APIs - **Serverless**: Lambda functions, Cloud Functions, Vercel Functions - **Hybrid**: Mixed patterns (e.g., Firebase + custom API endpoints). Extract indicators from keywords, dependencies, and architecture description. Document implications for services (client-side vs server-side), security model (rules vs middleware), and API layer requirements. Store pattern in metadata.architecturePattern from tool detection.

apiSpecification.title: API Specification (API-First Approach)
apiSpecification.description: Define API contracts and endpoints before implementation

endpoints.title: API Endpoints
endpoints.instruction: Define RESTful/GraphQL endpoints: - **GET /api/v1/resource** — [Description, parameters, response] - **POST /api/v1/resource** — [Description, request body, response] - **PUT /api/v1/resource/{id}** — [Description, parameters, request body, response] - **DELETE /api/v1/resource/{id}** — [Description, parameters, response]

contracts.title: API Contracts
contracts.instruction: Define request/response schemas: - **Request Schema**: [JSON schema for API requests] - **Response Schema**: [JSON schema for API responses] - **Error Schema**: [JSON schema for error responses] - **Validation Rules**: [Input validation requirements]

openApiSpec.title: OpenAPI Specification
openApiSpec.instruction: Generate OpenAPI 3.0 specification with: - API version and base URL - Authentication methods - All endpoints with full documentation - Request/response schemas - Error definitions - Examples for each endpoint

versioning.title: API Versioning Strategy
versioning.instruction: Define versioning approach: - **Versioning Method**: [URL path, header, query parameter] - **Version Lifecycle**: [Deprecation, sunset policies] - **Backward Compatibility**: [Breaking vs non-breaking changes] - **Migration Strategy**: [How clients migrate between versions]

testing.title: API Testing Strategy
testing.instruction: Define API testing approach: - **Contract Testing**: [Generated tests from OpenAPI spec] - **Integration Testing**: [End-to-end API testing] - **Performance Testing**: [Load testing requirements] - **Security Testing**: [Authentication, authorization, input validation]

simplicityGate.title: Simplicity Gate
simplicityGate.description: ≤ 10 projects for initial scope; otherwise, force simplification

libraryFirstGate.title: Library-First Gate
libraryFirstGate.description: Every feature starts as a standalone library (desktop/backend) or modular component (web/mobile/embedded). UI/app layers are thin veneers over core functionality

cliInterfaceGate.title: CLI Interface Gate
cliInterfaceGate.description: Each developer/system tool library exposes a CLI with --json mode using stdin/stdout; errors go to stderr

testFirstGate.title: Test-First Gate
testFirstGate.description: No implementation before tests; sequence is Contract → Integration → E2E → Unit → Implementation → UI-API Integration

antiAbstractionGate.title: Anti-Abstraction Gate
antiAbstractionGate.description: One domain model (avoid DTO/Repository/Unit-of-Work unless truly necessary)

traceabilityGate.title: Traceability Gate
traceabilityGate.description: Every line of code must trace back to a numbered requirement (FR-XXX) in the spec

nativeFirstGate.title: Native-First Gate
nativeFirstGate.description: Use platform-native capabilities and patterns. Avoid cross-platform frameworks unless justified

offlineFirstGate.title: Offline-First Gate
offlineFirstGate.description: Core functionality works without internet. Local data storage and sync when online

performanceGate.title: Performance Gate
performanceGate.description: Platform-specific performance requirements: Mobile (60fps, <3s launch, <100MB), Web (<3s load, <100ms interaction), Desktop (<2s startup, <50MB base)

accessibilityGate.title: Accessibility Gate
accessibilityGate.description: Full accessibility support: Mobile (screen reader, touch), Web (WCAG 2.1 AA), Desktop (OS accessibility features)

securityGate.title: Security Gate
securityGate.description: Platform-specific security: Mobile (encryption, secure storage), Web (HTTPS, CSP, XSS/CSRF), Backend (auth, validation), Desktop (code signing, sandboxing)

storeComplianceGate.title: Store Compliance Gate
storeComplianceGate.description: App store guidelines and review readiness for mobile apps

progressiveEnhancementGate.title: Progressive Enhancement Gate
progressiveEnhancementGate.description: Works without JavaScript, then enhances with JS. Graceful degradation

responsiveDesignGate.title: Responsive Design Gate
responsiveDesignGate.description: Mobile-first design with breakpoints for tablet and desktop. All screen sizes supported

browserCompatibilityGate.title: Browser Compatibility Gate
browserCompatibilityGate.description: Works on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. 95% of target browsers supported

nativeIntegrationGate.title: Native Integration Gate
nativeIntegrationGate.description: Integrate with OS features: menus, notifications, file associations, system preferences

distributionGate.title: Distribution Gate
distributionGate.description: Installer, auto-updates, and uninstaller. Code signing and update mechanisms

apiFirstGate.title: API-First Gate
apiFirstGate.description: RESTful/GraphQL APIs with OpenAPI specs. API documentation and versioning. All features expose well-defined APIs

databaseGate.title: Database Gate
databaseGate.description: Proper schema design, migrations, indexing, and data integrity

monitoringGate.title: Monitoring Gate
monitoringGate.description: Logging, metrics, health checks, and observability

dataQualityGate.title: Data Quality Gate
dataQualityGate.description: Clean, validated, representative datasets. Data preprocessing and validation

modelPerformanceGate.title: Model Performance Gate
modelPerformanceGate.description: Accuracy, precision, recall metrics. Model evaluation and benchmarking

reproducibilityGate.title: Reproducibility Gate
reproducibilityGate.description: Deterministic training, version control, and experiment tracking

ethicsGate.title: Ethics Gate
ethicsGate.description: Bias detection, fairness, explainability, and ethical AI principles

deploymentGate.title: Deployment Gate
deploymentGate.description: Model serving, monitoring, rollback, and production deployment

contentQuality.title: Content Quality
items: Focused on user value and business needs

constitutionalCompliance.title: Constitutional Compliance
items: Library-First approach planned (standalone library, thin UI veneer)
CLI interface planned (--json mode, stdin/stdout, stderr errors) for developer/system tools
Test-First approach planned (Contract → Integration → E2E → Unit → Implementation → UI-API Integration)
Integration-First testing planned (real dependencies, justify mocks)
Anti-Abstraction approach planned (single domain model, avoid DTO/Repository/Unit-of-Work)

beforeImplementation.title: Before ANY Implementation
items: Constitutional gates must pass or be justified in Complexity Tracking

duringImplementation.title: During Implementation
items: Fail early on violations; fix before proceeding

qualityChecks.title: Quality Gates
items: Full traceability from FR-XXX → tests → code

complexityTracking.title: Complexity Tracking
complexityTracking.description: Use only when a constitutional gate is intentionally broken
complexityTracking.instruction: If any constitutional gate is violated, document: 1) What was violated, 2) Why it was necessary, 3) Why simpler alternatives won't work

sddPrinciples.intentBeforeMechanism: Intent before mechanism: what and why precede how
sddPrinciples.multiStepRefinement: Multi-step refinement over one-shot code generation
sddPrinciples.cliInterfaceMandate: Every developer/system tool capability has a CLI-style interface (stdin/stdout, JSON option)
sddPrinciples.libraryFirstPrinciple: Start as a standalone library (desktop/backend) or modular component (web/mobile/embedded)
sddPrinciples.testFirstImperative: No implementation before tests; sequence is Contract → Integration → E2E → Unit → Implementation
sddPrinciples.integrationFirstTesting: Prefer real dependencies (DBs/services). Mocks require written justification
sddPrinciples.simplicityConstraints: ≤ 10 projects at start; use framework features directly; document any complexity
sddPrinciples.antiAbstraction: One domain model (avoid DTO/Repository/Unit-of-Work unless truly necessary)
sddPrinciples.traceability: Every line of code must trace back to a numbered requirement (FR-XXX) in the spec
